audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for tradition of elders, heart/defilement teaching, Canaanite woman, healing summary, and feeding four thousand.

verses.restored: Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying,

familiar.text: Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying,

modern.text: Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked,

original.text: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων ⸂Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς⸃ λέγοντες

verses.restored: Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.

familiar.text: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.

modern.text: “Why do Your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands before they eat.”

original.text: Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων; οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας ⸀αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.

verses.restored: He answered them, Why do you also transgress the command of the Divine because of your tradition?

familiar.text: But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?

modern.text: Jesus replied, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν;

verses.restored: For the Divine said, Honor father and mother, and, The one speaking evil of father or mother must surely come to an end.

familiar.text: For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.

modern.text: For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’

original.text: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ⸀εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·

verses.restored: But you say, Whoever says to father or mother, Whatever you might have gained from me is a gift-offering,

familiar.text: But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me;

modern.text: But you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,’

original.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς,

verses.restored: he need not honor his father. So you have made the word of the Divine void because of your tradition.

familiar.text: And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.

modern.text: he need not honor his father or mother with it. Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition.

original.text: ⸀οὐ μὴ ⸀τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα ⸀αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε ⸂τὸν λόγον⸃ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied beautifully about you, saying:

familiar.text: Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying,

modern.text: You hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied correctly about you:

original.text: ὑποκριταί, καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων·

verses.restored: This people honors me with lips, but their heart is far away from me.

familiar.text: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.

modern.text: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.

original.text: ⸂Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος⸃ τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·

verses.restored: In vain they worship me, teaching as teachings the commands of humans.

familiar.text: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

modern.text: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’ ” What Defiles a Man (Mark 7:14–23)

original.text: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: Calling the crowd to him, he said to them, Hear and understand:

familiar.text: And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:

modern.text: Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “Listen and understand.

original.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε·

verses.restored: Not what enters the mouth makes a person common/unclean, but what comes out of the mouth; this makes a person common/unclean.

familiar.text: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.

modern.text: A man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it.”

original.text: οὐ τὸ εἰσερχόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: Then the disciples came and said to him, Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this word?

familiar.text: Then came his disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?

modern.text: Then the disciples came to Him and said, “Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?”

original.text: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ ⸀λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οἶδας ὅτι οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν;

verses.restored: He answered, Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.

familiar.text: But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται.

verses.restored: Leave them; they are blind guides. If blind guide blind, both will fall into a pit.

familiar.text: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.

modern.text: Disregard them! They are blind guides. If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.”

original.text: ἄφετε αὐτούς· ⸂τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοὶ τυφλῶν⸃· τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ, ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον πεσοῦνται.

verses.restored: Peter answered him, Explain this parable to us.

familiar.text: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Declare unto us this parable.

modern.text: Peter said to Him, “Explain this parable to us.”

original.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Φράσον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν ⸀ταύτην.

verses.restored: He said, Are you also still without understanding?

familiar.text: And Jesus said, Are ye also yet without understanding?

modern.text: “Do you still not understand?” Jesus asked.

original.text: ὁ ⸀δὲ εἶπεν· Ἀκμὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε;

verses.restored: Do you not perceive that everything entering the mouth goes into the belly and is passed out?

familiar.text: Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?

modern.text: “Do you not yet realize that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated?

original.text: ⸀οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν χωρεῖ καὶ εἰς ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται;

verses.restored: But the things coming out of the mouth come out from the heart, and those make a person common/unclean.

familiar.text: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.

modern.text: But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man.

original.text: τὰ δὲ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχεται, κἀκεῖνα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: For from the heart come harmful reasonings, murders, adulteries, sexual unfaithfulness, thefts, false witness, slanders.

familiar.text: For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:

modern.text: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.

original.text: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί, φόνοι, μοιχεῖαι, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, ψευδομαρτυρίαι, βλασφημίαι.

verses.restored: These are what make a person common/unclean; but eating with unwashed hands does not make a person common/unclean.

familiar.text: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.

modern.text: These are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him.” The Faith of the Canaanite Woman (Mark 7:24–30)

original.text: ταῦτά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον, τὸ δὲ ἀνίπτοις χερσὶν φαγεῖν οὐ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: Jesus went away from there and withdrew into the regions of Tyre and Sidon.

familiar.text: Then Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.

modern.text: Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon.

original.text: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος.

verses.restored: And look, a Canaanite woman from those borders came out and cried, Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is badly troubled.

familiar.text: And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.

modern.text: And a Canaanite woman from that region came to Him, crying out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.”

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ Χαναναία ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων ἐκείνων ἐξελθοῦσα ⸀ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Ἐλέησόν με, κύριε ⸀υἱὸς Δαυίδ· ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται.

verses.restored: But he did not answer her a word. His disciples came and urged him, saying, Release her, because she cries out after us.

familiar.text: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.

modern.text: But Jesus did not answer a word. So His disciples came and urged Him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῇ λόγον. καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀ἠρώτουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον αὐτήν, ὅτι κράζει ὄπισθεν ἡμῶν.

verses.restored: He answered, I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

familiar.text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

modern.text: He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.

verses.restored: But she came and bowed/prostrated before him, saying, Lord, help me.

familiar.text: Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.

modern.text: The woman came and knelt before Him. “Lord, help me!” she said.

original.text: ἡ δὲ ἐλθοῦσα ⸀προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγουσα· Κύριε, βοήθει μοι.

verses.restored: He answered, It is not beautiful/good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.

familiar.text: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔστιν καλὸν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις.

verses.restored: She said, Yes, Lord; yet even the little dogs eat from the crumbs falling from their masters' table.

familiar.text: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.

modern.text: “Yes, Lord,” she said, “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”

original.text: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, κύριε, καὶ γὰρ τὰ κυνάρια ἐσθίει ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τῶν κυρίων αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: Then Jesus answered her, O woman, great is your trust; let it happen for you as you desire. And her daughter was healed from that hour.

familiar.text: Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.

modern.text: “O woman,” Jesus answered, “your faith is great! Let it be done for you as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that very hour. The Feeding of the Four Thousand (2 Kings 4:42–44; Mark 8:1–10)

original.text: τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Ὦ γύναι, μεγάλη σου ἡ πίστις· γενηθήτω σοι ὡς θέλεις. καὶ ἰάθη ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.

verses.restored: Departing from there, Jesus came beside the Sea of Galilee, went up the mountain, and sat there.

familiar.text: And Jesus departed from thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee; and went up into a mountain, and sat down there.

modern.text: Moving on from there, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee. Then He went up on a mountain and sat down.

original.text: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἀναβὰς εἰς τὸ ὄρος ἐκάθητο ἐκεῖ.

verses.restored: Great crowds came to him, having with them the lame, blind, crippled, mute, and many others; they laid them at his feet, and he healed them.

familiar.text: And great multitudes came unto him, having with them those that were lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and cast them down at Jesus’ feet; and he healed them:

modern.text: Large crowds came to Him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and laid them at His feet, and He healed them.

original.text: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἔχοντες μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν ⸂κωφούς, τυφλούς, χωλούς, κυλλούς⸃, καὶ ἑτέρους πολλούς, καὶ ἔρριψαν αὐτοὺς παρὰ τοὺς πόδας ⸀αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς·

verses.restored: So the crowd marveled, seeing mute people speaking, crippled people whole, lame people walking, and blind people seeing; and they glorified the Divine of Israel.

familiar.text: Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.

modern.text: The crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.

original.text: ὥστε ⸂τὸν ὄχλον⸃ θαυμάσαι βλέποντας κωφοὺς λαλοῦντας ⸂κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς⸃ ⸀καὶ χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας καὶ τυφλοὺς βλέποντας· καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν Ἰσραήλ.

verses.restored: Jesus called his disciples and said, I am moved with compassion for the crowd, because they remain with me three days and have nothing to eat; I do not want to release them hungry, lest they faint on the way.

familiar.text: Then Jesus called his disciples unto him, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.

modern.text: Then Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way.”

original.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν· καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτοὺς νήστεις οὐ θέλω, μήποτε ἐκλυθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

verses.restored: The disciples said to him, From where in a deserted place are there enough loaves for us to satisfy so great a crowd?

familiar.text: And his disciples say unto him, Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude?

modern.text: The disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd?”

original.text: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ ⸀μαθηταί· Πόθεν ἡμῖν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ ἄρτοι τοσοῦτοι ὥστε χορτάσαι ὄχλον τοσοῦτον;

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, How many loaves do you have? They said, Seven, and a few little fish.

familiar.text: And Jesus saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a few little fishes.

modern.text: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied, “and a few small fish.”

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά, καὶ ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια.

verses.restored: Commanding the crowd to recline on the ground,

familiar.text: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground.

modern.text: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground.

original.text: καὶ ⸀παραγγείλας ⸂τῷ ὄχλῳ⸃ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν

verses.restored: he took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.

familiar.text: And he took the seven loaves and the fishes, and gave thanks, and brake them, and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.

modern.text: Taking the seven loaves and the fish, He gave thanks and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.

original.text: ⸀ἔλαβεν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς ἰχθύας ⸀καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸀ἐδίδου τοῖς ⸀μαθηταῖς οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ⸂τοῖς ὄχλοις⸃.

verses.restored: They all ate and were filled, and they took up what remained of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.

familiar.text: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.

modern.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

original.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ⸂τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων ἦραν⸃ ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας πλήρεις.

verses.restored: Those eating were four thousand men, besides women and children.

familiar.text: And they that did eat were four thousand men, beside women and children.

modern.text: A total of four thousand men were fed, in addition to women and children.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν τετρακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.

verses.restored: After releasing the crowds, he entered the boat and came into the borders of Magadan.

familiar.text: And he sent away the multitude, and took ship, and came into the coasts of Magdala.

modern.text: After Jesus had dismissed the crowds, He got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.

original.text: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια ⸀Μαγαδάν.
